definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese confection consisting of a flat rice cake filled with sweet bean paste and wrapped in an oak leaf. Eaten during Children's Day (May 5).

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{柏餅|かしわもち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: We eat kashiwa mochi on Children's Day.

examples.japanese: {和菓子屋|わがしや}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{柏餅|かしわもち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}って→買う：00489_kau⟧きた。
examples.english: I bought kashiwa mochi from a Japanese confectionery shop.

examples.japanese: ⟦{柏|かしわ}→柏：26146_kashiwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{新芽|しんめ}→新芽：13028_shinme⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{落|お}ちない→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、{柏餅|かしわもち}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{子孫|しそん}→子孫：00372_shison⟧⟦{繁栄|はんえい}→繁栄：10131_hanei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{縁起物|えんぎもの}→縁起物：15731_engimono⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Because oak leaves don't fall until new buds appear, kashiwa mochi is considered a good-luck charm for the prosperity of one's descendants.

notes:
A seasonal Japanese sweet closely associated with ⟦{端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく}→端午の節句：16518_tangonosekku⟧ (Boys' Day / Children's Day, May 5). The oak leaf (⟦{柏|かしわ}→柏：26146_kashiwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧) wrapping is symbolic: because oak trees hold their old leaves until new growth appears, the leaf represents the continuity of family lineage.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditionally eaten on May 5th as part of Children's Day celebrations. The filling is typically ⟦{餡子|あんこ}→餡子：08654_anko⟧ (sweet red bean paste), though {味噌餡|みそあん} (sweet miso paste) is also common. The leaf is not eaten — it serves as a wrapper and imparts a subtle aroma.
